charts.title: Commercial OEM vs Aftermarket vs Defense
charts.annotation: Defense is sold direct to governments and prime contractors; the two commercial lines track OEM build rates and the much higher-margin spares/overhaul aftermarket.

charts.title: Organic vs. Acquired Revenue Growth
charts.annotation: Organic + acquisition growth approximates total revenue growth; FX and divestitures are the usual small residual.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue
segmentRevenue.content:
TransDigm reports three segments: Power & Control (power generation/conversion, motion control, fluid power), Airframe (structural components, cockpit/cabin systems) and a small Non-aviation business. Nearly all growth and most acquisitions land in Power & Control and Airframe.

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: Power & Control is now the larger segment and carries the DCF's assumed margin mix; a shift between segments changes the blended EBITDA margin even if total revenue is unchanged.

What to watch:

  • Which segment is absorbing new acquisitions
  • Non-aviation's size (negligible, but a reminder this is a diversified industrial, not a pure aerospace play)

segmentMargin.title: Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin
segmentMargin.content:
Each segment's Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of its own revenue -- TransDigm's own disclosed, non-GAAP measure (add-backs for purchase-accounting and refinancing items), not derivable from the blended EBITDA column.

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: Power & Control and Airframe both run mid-50s% margins on proprietary, sole-source aftermarket parts; Non-aviation runs far lower and is not the margin driver.

What to watch:

  • Margin compression in either core segment (pricing power eroding)
  • Acquisitions diluting segment margin before integration pricing is applied

commercialMix.title: Commercial OEM vs Aftermarket vs Defense
commercialMix.content:
Revenue split by end market: Commercial OEM (new aircraft production), Commercial Aftermarket (spares and overhaul on the installed fleet) and Defense (military programs, largely cost-plus or sole-source).

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: aftermarket is the highest-margin, most resilient stream -- it tracks flight hours on an installed base that takes decades to turn over, not current-year aircraft deliveries. Defense provides a counter-cycle buffer when commercial OEM build rates fall.

What to watch:

  • Aftermarket growing faster than OEM (installed-base effect, margin-accretive)
  • Defense share rising in a commercial downturn

organicAcquired.title: Organic vs. acquired growth
organicAcquired.content:
Organic growth is revenue growth from existing businesses; acquisition growth is the contribution from businesses bought in the trailing twelve months, both as management discloses them.

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: disciplined M&A of proprietary, sole-source aerospace component makers is the other half of the growth algorithm alongside organic aftermarket/OEM growth -- the DCF's revenue path blends both, so a quarter where acquisitions dominate is not the same quality of growth as organic share gains.

What to watch:

  • Acquisition contribution fading as deals anniversary into the organic base after 12 months
  • Years with unusually large acquisition contribution (deployment of the highly leveraged balance sheet)

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For TransDigm Group Incorporated: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
